If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment swings from positive to negative over last 5 days, shift forecast downward by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price has been trending upward, reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% in late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent overextension.

If sentiment is neutral and price has been trending downward, increase forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid premature bottoming.

If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >1.5% from true path, apply a 0.5–1.0% correction in mid-horizon to dampen erratic behavior.
